title: Beneath School diversity, three Roman agreements: some cult owed; rightly called adoratio; bodily honors licit
source_text: XI. Sed quicquid sit de ista sententiarum in Schola Romana diversitate, omnes ejus Doctores in eo, ut saepius jam dictum, conveniunt: 1. Cultum aliquem imaginibus Christi & Sanctorum esse deferendum. 2. Cultum illum adorationis vocabulo recte significari posse. 3. Cultum illum legitime exhiberi, coram imaginibus caput aperiendo, & genua flectendo, ipsisque luminaria & thura offerendo.
pass_a_gloss: But whatever may be of that diversity of opinions in the Roman School, all its Doctors agree in this, as has already been said often: 1. That some cult is to be paid to the images of Christ and of the Saints. 2. That that cult can rightly be signified by the vocabulary of adoration. 3. That that cult is legitimately exhibited by uncovering the head before images, and bending the knee, and offering to them lights and incense.
pass_b_english: Diversity aside, Rome’s Doctors lock three points: some cult is owed to the images; adoratio is the right word; uncovering, kneeling, lights, and incense are legitimate.
